Third development release of 0.17.0: DIN-rail cabinets, racks in 3D with their ports live on the elevation, drawings that export to SVG and PDF, MAC tracking on switch ports, and the fixes reported against dev2.

> [!CAUTION]
> This is a development release, and bugs are expected. If you run into one, you are welcome to [submit a bug report](https://github.com/danbyte-net/danbyte/issues/new?template=bug_report.md) - every report helps get 0.17.0 right.

### DIN-rail cabinets (#277)

- **Cabinets** are a new place to mount devices, next to racks: a control cabinet's mounting plate with its DIN rails (TS 35, TS 15, G 32), for PLCs, industrial switches, power supplies and other DIN gear. Cabinets have types (sizes and rails copied on create; *Sync from type* adds or moves rails and never removes one), coloured roles, statuses, tags, custom fields, images, documents, a journal and a change log, and a Cabinets tab on sites and locations.
- **Mounting.** A device type gets its body size in millimetres and the rail profiles it fits; a device sits on a rail at an offset. The device form draws the cabinet: click, drag, nudge or slide the device along a rail; the offset starts at the first gap it fits. Rails, cabinets and types refuse a change their devices would not survive. The cabinet page's **Arrange** moves several devices in one save, and the server checks the whole arrangement before it writes.
- **True-size photos.** Calibrate a photo in the photo editor - two guides a known distance apart and the rail line - and the plate draws it at its real size, as does the Diagram's *Own size*. The plate has the rack's looks - *Names*, *Images* and *Render* (live faceplates with their ports) - with labels, zoom and an export.
- **3D.** The cabinet page has a **2D | 3D** switch: the enclosure with a door that opens onto the plate, its rails and each device at true size with its photo and coloured ports. Floor plans link a tile to a cabinet: the tile counts its devices and rolls up their monitoring, cables to its devices end on it, a click opens a panel with the plate, and **Show on floor plan** finds it. In the 3D room the cabinet stands as a closed box whose door opens the same way.

### Racks (#248)

- **The rack page** keeps its facts on the left and draws the rack on the right, with a **2D | 3D** switch. In 2D the zoom fits front and rear side by side; 3D shows this rack alone with its photo faceplates and coloured ports, with **Front**, **Rear** and **PNG**; cables are not drawn there yet.
- **Live ports on the elevation.** *Render* and *Images* draw each device's ports as its device page does - cabled by speed, free, reserved, disabled - from one request for the whole rack. Every device shows its ports in use (`38 / 48`, with a tip saying what counts), a cabled port opens its trace, and **Capacity** gains *Free* and *Ports* (linking to Port utilization for the rack). The port hover card gains a **Far end** line, on the device page too.
- **Full-depth gear shows its other side.** On the rear elevation a full-depth server draws its rear photo or drawing - NICs and PSUs included, live - instead of hatching; it stays hatched only when there is no image for that side.
- **Display menu** on the rack and the cabinet: Text, **Ports** (off draws bare photos and the plain drawing) and, on racks, **Show** all, front-mounted or rear-mounted devices; hidden devices stay hatched so used and free space read right.
- **Part status from any photo view.** A disk, PSU or fan marker's card lists its statuses as pills, and a right click opens the same choices - on the device page, the rack and cabinet drawings and in 3D.

### Export

- **Rack and cabinet drawings export to PNG, SVG and PDF**, like the topology: the files are drawn from the data, not snapped from the screen, and the PDF lays the drawing out on A4, A3, Letter or Tabloid under a title block the server writes (rack portrait, cabinet landscape by default), with a Print entry. The topology's PDF now shares the same renderer.

### MAC tracking (#284)

- **Switch ports show the devices behind them.** SNMP now reads a switch's MAC address table vendor-neutrally - Q-BRIDGE-MIB with each entry's VLAN, BRIDGE-MIB as the fallback, and the per-VLAN tables some switches keep (`community@vlan`, or the `vlan-N` context for SNMPv3) - keeps learned entries only, so a port's own MAC no longer shows, and maps each one to its real port. A switch that reads a table shows **Learned MACs** per port on its SNMP tab and under Components → Interfaces (the whole-stack table too): each MAC with its name and IP, `+N more`, and a count on an uplink. A line under the table says how the last read went.
- **Uplinks** are told apart by an LLDP switch neighbour (an IP phone does not count), a LAG, more learned MACs than *Uplink above*, or the interface's own **Uplink: Automatic / Always / Never**, in its form and in bulk edit. An interface gets a **MACs** tab with what it learned, present or all.
- **Where is this MAC?** The MAC page shows its **Location** (switch, port, VLAN, since when), **IP** (from ARP, DHCP or a paired address) and **Name** (a Danbyte interface or MAC object, else DNS or DHCP), and **Observed** lists every port and ARP table that saw it. `/macs` gains a **Learned** tab: one row per MAC at its location, filtered by site, device, VLAN and state. A MAC pasted into search in any notation shows the port it was learned on.
- **History.** Each MAC on each port and VLAN keeps its first and last seen; a MAC that disappears stays as history for *Forget MACs unseen for* (30 days).
- **Refresh MACs** re-reads a switch's whole table in the background, from its SNMP tab or Components.
- **Settings:** a **MAC tracking** card on Settings → Monitoring (MACs shown per port, Uplink above, LLDP switch neighbours mark uplinks, Forget MACs unseen for), and **Per-VLAN MAC tables** (Auto / Always / Off) on SNMP profiles.
- **Outposts** need **danbyte-outpost 0.9.0** to send VLANs and per-VLAN tables; older agents keep working the old way, and their empty tables never mark a MAC gone.

### Upgrading

- **Package updates no longer break an upgrade.** On a host that just booted, the system's own updates can restart PostgreSQL in the middle of a migration. The upgrade now waits for them, up to 20 minutes, before it stops anything, and a migration that loses its database to a restart and rolled back in full runs once more. `install.sh` waits for the package lock instead of failing.
- **The upgrade's run folder and database snapshot are private** to the service account (#281). Any local user could read the snapshot while the upgrade ran, and for as long as a failed restore kept it; the next upgrade closes up folders an earlier run left.
- An upgrade with nothing to migrate that fails afterwards rolls back only the code, instead of trying to restore a snapshot it never took and leaving Danbyte stopped (#278).
- A successful upgrade removes the folder an earlier failed run kept for its log.
- The installer's root steps no longer write two journal lines every two seconds while they wait, and its failure summary keeps the quotes in an error message.
- The fast lane reconnects after a database restart instead of failing every write until it is restarted.

### Fixed

- **A site certificate upload could replace another site's certificate** on a shared nginx (#279). The apply unit and `danbyte-admin tls` took the first certificate in the whole nginx configuration; they now read only Danbyte's own site, refuse when nginx does not load it, and leave a certificate tool's links (certbot's `live/`) alone. `danbyte-admin tls self-signed` no longer collects other sites' names.
- **Bulk delete and bulk update answered 500** for ids that are not ids or a body that is not an object (#280); they answer 400 with the reason, on every list.
- **LLDP links to a switch stack were drawn once per member** (#283); a stack's links are drawn once, on the member that owns the port.
- **Bulk delete** collected each row on its own (#282). Its preview now costs the same whatever the number of rows, and the delete about half as much per row, removing the free rows together.
- Dashboards and monitoring filters answer 400 instead of 500 for ids that are not ids (#273), SLA burn rates for numbers that are not finite (#274), and the topology API reads a depth too large to parse as any other unreadable depth (#275). A deleted home dashboard no longer opens from the menu (#269), and dashboard monitoring widgets stay empty without IP view (#268).
- SLA month, quarter and year to date start at local midnight (#270), and daily rollups keep their spikes (#271).
- The 0.17 upgrade's *Kept user management* grant gave every holder all the verbs any of them had; it is split by account now (#272).
- The API refuses a status the catalog does not offer that object type, in single and bulk edits, as the forms always did.
- A status's usage counts its cabinets, and its IPs tab shows its own count instead of the status's total.
- SNMP interface samples are pruned after three days; nothing pruned them before.
- Saving an SNMP profile keeps the settings its form has no field for; it dropped them.
- Device photos under 2000 px are stored as uploaded. Every one was re-encoded, and *Resize* saved a new copy of a face already within the size asked for.

### Security

- **An import could reference another tenant's ports.** A MAC address row could name another tenant's interface, and any port or VM interface reference likewise; an import now resolves them through their parent inside the active tenant, as the API fields do.
- **An Outpost writes SNMP results only for the devices it polls.** The core took results for any device in the Outpost's tenant; with learned MACs and ARP in those results, an agent's token could have written sightings for another site's switch.

### Also new

- **Port counting** is one rule everywhere - device and stack cards, Port utilization, spec sheets, alerts and racks: physical interfaces and front ports, virtual interfaces only when **Count virtual interfaces** is on (Settings → Component details), rear ports never. Virtual, bridge and LAG interfaces are flagged virtual (#247).
- Detail pages show their figures in the Overview cards instead of a strip under the title.
- Settings → **Monitoring** moves from Notifications to **Devices & polling**, beside SNMP profiles and sensors.
- **Space map:** rows past eight bits draw as strips (point for the subnet, click to zoom in), a prefix inside a master zooms out one bit at a time or to any size up to the master, and **Aligned** draws each row on one line under the blocks it splits.
- Tunnels take a capacity (`capacity_kbps`, API only for now) for the site map's link speeds (#246).
